title: Speed vs Accuracy Trade-off Mastery
tagline: Year 4 — Finding the pace that maximises score when faster means less accurate, with and without negative marking

introduction.overview: Going faster lets you attempt more questions but usually lowers accuracy; going slower raises accuracy but reduces attempts. The best pace is the one that maximises correct answers (minus penalties). If you measure your accuracy at several paces in mocks, you can compute the score for each and choose. This chapter uses a hypothetical accuracy table to teach the method: score = attempts × accuracy for no penalty, and attempts × (accuracy − penalty × (1 − accuracy)) with a penalty. The rules and figures used in examples are hypothetical teaching rules, not the policy of any real company or platform.
introduction.placementRelevance: Finding your own optimal pace is the most personal and most valuable strategic exercise.
introduction.realWorldContext: Balancing speed and quality is a standard trade-off in professional work.

learningObjectives: Compute attempts at a given pace
Compute expected correct answers and net marks
Compare paces and choose the best
See how penalties shift the best pace
Measure your own accuracy at different paces

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Attempts = time ÷ pace. Correct = attempts × accuracy. Net = correct − penalty × wrong.

coreDefinitions: Accuracy curve: accuracy at each pace.
Optimal pace: pace with the highest net marks.
Sensitivity: how much the result changes with pace.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: The best pace balances two curves: more attempts and falling accuracy.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: For each pace compute attempts, correct and net; pick the highest.

mainNarrative: Hypothetical accuracy table (3,600 seconds available): 60 s gives 70% accuracy, 75 s gives 80%, 90 s gives 88%, 120 s gives 92%.
Attempts: 60, 48, 40, 30. Correct: 42, 38.4, 35.2, 27.6. With no penalty, 60 s is best (42).
Measure your own accuracy curve on mocks before choosing a pace.

deepDiveAspects.title: Plateau
deepDiveAspects.content: Beyond a certain pace extra time barely raises accuracy.

deepDiveAspects.title: Question mix
deepDiveAspects.content: Easy questions have a flatter curve; hard questions a steeper one.
